newsitem.title: USA: Guidant says launches Ventak AV in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Guidant says launches Ventak AV in U.S.

text.p: Guidant Corp said Monday it launched U.S. marketing of its Ventak AV implantable defibrillator, which was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

The medical device is expected by analysts to boost Guidant's presence in the fast-growing world market for implantable defibrillators, or ICDs, which are placed in the body and wire to the heart to keep it from beating too fast.
The Ventak AV combines traditional ICD functions with dual-chamber pacemaker therapy, Guidant said.

"The expanded treatment options that the Ventak AV system can provide to patients at risk for life-threatening arrhythmias is significant," said Jay Graf, president of Guidant's cardiac rhythm management group.

"The Ventak AV system was the world's first integration of dual-chamber pacing therapy and advanced defibrillation therapy. We are pleased to be the first company to bring an advanced defibrillation system of this type for commercial use in the United States as well," Graf said.
